lines: You've probably heard of Grok Bot.
But here is what actually makes it different from every other personal agent.
Most personal agents work the same way. You talk to one agent.
It can spin off different threads or channels, but everything still happens through a single conversation.
Talk about ads, email and projects all at once, and things get convoluted and confusing.
With Grok Bot, you get a separate bot for every job.
Instead of one assistant, you build a whole team of bots.
Each one has its own role.
Creating one is simple. Give it a name, pick an avatar, and define its role.
Whatever you want it to be.
Say you run ads. One bot only handles your Meta Ads.
Another is your Google Ads manager. Another is your project manager.
When a topic comes up, you already know exactly who to talk to.
Segmenting your bots like this keeps every conversation clean.
Still prefer a single thread? There's a chief of staff bot.
It's the most proactive of the group, and it delegates work out to all the other bots.
So you talk to one bot, and still get a whole team working.
Every bot can have its own mailbox.
And when it needs access to something, it asks for your approval through one password, instead of asking you to paste secrets into a chat.
It also plugs into a large library of connectors, so your bots can work inside the tools you already use.
Here's a standout feature. Grok Bot can make phone calls for you.
Need a restaurant reservation? Or want to change your internet plan without sitting on hold for forty five minutes?
Your bot makes the call, waits on the line, and dials you in only when a real person answers.
It even reaches your car. Connect your Tesla, and the same bot from your app comes along for the ride.
Ask about your emails, or check on a workflow, without ever opening your laptop.
Grok Bot. A team of bots, one for every job.
Based on a review by Thomas Bekkers.
